page_title: Content Factory: Free Faceless Video Generator for Mac

summary.name: Content Factory
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source Mac app that turns a script into a finished faceless "What if" short video using AI-generated stills, parallax motion, narration, subtitles and music.
use_cases: Make faceless What if shorts for TikTok, YouTube Shorts or Instagram Reels
Turn a written script into a narrated video with subtitles without editing
Generate short videos from stills without paying per video
Let Claude write and render a video over MCP
Produce illustrated SVG-style shorts with no stock images
summary.what_it_does: Takes a script (written by the user or by Claude via MCP) and produces a 9:16 short video of 30 to 120 seconds. It generates one still per beat, adds depth parallax, RIFE transitions and camera moves without a video model, and narrates with Kokoro on MLX with loudness set to -14 LUFS. Word-by-word subtitles come from Whisper alignment, with CC0 music ducked under the voice. Remotion renders the result and a check covers length, black frames, loudness and text before the user accepts it. Only image prompts leave the Mac, sent to a provider the user chooses with their own key.
notable: Open source under MIT on GitHub, with no video model; motion made from stills on the Mac
MCP server lets Claude Code or other MCP clients write scripts and run the pipeline
Drawn mode has Claude paint each beat as SVG in styles like gouache, ink, crayon or flat vector, with no image provider needed
Cached pipeline stages so editing one line re-voices only that beat
caveats: Requires Apple silicon Mac; Windows and Linux are planned, not available
No signed download yet; must be built from source with uv, Node.js 20+, FFmpeg and Rust
Image generation requires the user's own API key with OpenAI, Google or fal.ai, billed separately
Built-in narration is English (Kokoro) with Russian via optional Vosk voice; Higgsfield comparison figures are Higgsfield's own estimates
